channel: More tokens can be served by better models, so efficiency substitutes for raw capacity.
condition: Model efficiency improves faster than usage grows.
assumption: Efficiency gains are absorbed by new uses rather than reducing capacity demand.
kill: Capacity demand falls in absolute terms while token volume rises.

channel: Volume growth at falling prices is the evidence that demand is elastic.
condition: Price and volume move in opposite directions in the same window.
assumption: Observed volume growth is measurable independent of price changes.
kill: Volume falls while price falls.

channel: Falling unit prices pull new workloads into production.
condition: Elasticity above one at the current price point.
assumption: Demand for inference is elastic and unused cases exist at lower prices.
kill: Token spend falls when price per token falls.

channel: Agents keep consuming when a human session would have ended.
condition: Agent products run continuously rather than per request.
assumption: Always-on workloads lift the utilisation floor rather than the peak.
kill: Agent traffic is spiky and does not change the floor.

channel: Frontier runs reserve capacity far ahead, lengthening quoted lead times.
condition: A small number of very large commitments dominate the order book.
assumption: Training demand is concentrated enough to clear the vendor backlog.
kill: Lead times shorten while training commitments grow.

channel: More served tokens pull memory bits through the same fabs.
condition: Memory content per accelerator rises with model size.
assumption: HBM capacity is the binding constraint on accelerator shipments.
kill: Accelerator shipments rise while HBM supply is flat.

channel: Continuous inference load raises the peak and the floor of power demand at once.
condition: Load is firm rather than interruptible.
assumption: Data centre load does not curtail at system peaks.
kill: Firm capacity prices stay flat while data centre load grows.

channel: Export rules push sovereign buyers toward domestic or licensed capacity.
condition: Controls bind on the specific part numbers the buyer needs.
assumption: Sovereign demand exists and is funded.
kill: Sovereign programmes are announced and never built.

channel: Isolated national sites often bring their own generation.
condition: Grid connection is unavailable on the programme schedule.
assumption: On site generation clears the permit faster than the queue.
kill: Sovereign sites wait for the grid and cancel generation.

channel: Cheaper tokens per wait soften the urgency of new connections.
condition: Efficiency gains arrive before the connection is needed.
assumption: Efficiency gains are not immediately absorbed by new demand.
kill: Efficiency improves and power demand for the same workload rises.

channel: A cluster needs silicon and power in the same window; the shorter of the two decides.
condition: Both inputs are required before the site earns revenue.
assumption: Silicon and power lead times are comparable and not substitutable.
kill: Clusters energise with siloed silicon or idle powered sites without silicon.

channel: Memory constrained supply keeps rental prices firm for installed capacity.
condition: Installed capacity is scarce relative to demand.
assumption: Rental price clears on availability rather than on cost.
kill: Rental prices fall while accelerator shipments are constrained.

channel: Packaging lines gate finished accelerators even when wafers are available.
condition: Packaging is a separate bottleneck from wafer capacity.
assumption: Packaging capacity does not expand as fast as wafer capacity.
kill: Lead times shorten while packaging capacity is flat.

channel: In-house silicon reduces the future demand for merchant parts and their resale value.
condition: The substitute reaches production at scale.
assumption: ASIC programmes replace rather than complement merchant parts.
kill: Resale values hold while substitution scales.

channel: Resale value is the collateral story that securitisation depends on.
condition: Deals are underwritten against residual value.
assumption: Residual value is measurable and financeable.
kill: Securitisation spreads do not move with residual values.

channel: Residual prices are the outside evidence on useful life.
condition: An active secondary market exists.
assumption: Depreciation policy is a judgment that the market can contradict.
kill: Reported useful life and market residual values diverge without any consequence.

channel: Restricted buyers accelerate their own programmes.
condition: Controls bind on merchant parts for that buyer.
assumption: The buyer has the scale and talent to build its own part.
kill: Restricted buyers keep buying merchant silicon through third parties.

channel: Optics determine how far compute can sit from users at a given latency.
condition: Latency budget is the constraint rather than cost.
assumption: Latency requirements are stable across the workload set.
kill: Workloads tolerate any distance and geography stops mattering.

channel: Queue position is the clock on the project.
condition: The queue is processed in order rather than by fast track.
assumption: Queue positions are real and not reordered by policy.
kill: Projects jump the queue without paying or a rule change.

channel: Reform shortens the study phase and clears backlogs.
condition: Reform is implemented rather than filed.
assumption: Reform targets the binding step rather than the easy one.
kill: Queue times are unchanged after reform is implemented.

channel: New turbines add dispatchable capacity, easing scarcity later.
condition: Slots convert to operating plants.
assumption: Slot bookings are not cancelled by financing or permits.
kill: Scarcity persists after booked slots are delivered.

channel: Auction clearing is the priced version of scarcity.
condition: Auction and energy markets clear the same reliability product.
assumption: Prices reflect scarcity rather than administratively capped values.
kill: Auction clears low while energy prices spike.

channel: High merchant prices make self generation cheaper than the grid.
condition: On site generation is permitted and fuelled.
assumption: The load can build generation faster than it can buy power.
kill: Loads pay record prices and build nothing.

channel: Long dated nuclear contracts convert scarcity into contracted supply.
condition: Plants extend or restart rather than retire.
assumption: Contract volumes are additional rather than reshuffled.
kill: Scarcity persists while nuclear PPAs are signed for existing volumes.

channel: Behind the meter load never joins the queue.
condition: Permitting allows on site generation at scale.
assumption: On site capacity is large enough to matter to the queue.
kill: Queue growth continues at the same rate while self generation scales.

channel: Pass through contracts let providers offer fixed prices and win longer commitments.
condition: Tenants value price certainty.
assumption: Providers are willing to pass through rather than absorb energy risk.
kill: Tenants refuse pass through and demand fixed all in pricing.

channel: Delay keeps installed capacity scarce and rental spreads wide.
condition: Demand outruns connections.
assumption: The bottleneck is real rather than announced.
kill: Spreads narrow while energization delays lengthen.

channel: Scarcity forces utilities to plan capacity and grid work.
condition: Utilities are the ones who build the response.
assumption: Regulators allow the recovery of the spend.
kill: Capex plans shrink while scarcity is priced higher.

channel: Cluster studies and automation cut the study backlog.
condition: The bottleneck is study labour rather than siting.
assumption: Study capacity can be expanded with process rather than people.
kill: Backlog grows while reform is claimed implemented.

channel: No transformer means no energization, whatever the queue says.
condition: Transformer delivery precedes energization.
assumption: The transformer is a true gate rather than a schedulable input.
kill: Sites energize without transformers or with substitutes.

channel: Equipment scarcity forces plans to stretch and rephase.
condition: Plans are equipment constrained rather than budget constrained.
assumption: Utilities cannot substitute equipment or buy second hand at scale.
kill: Plans accelerate while lead times lengthen.

channel: Transformer lead times are the surface read on core steel tightness.
condition: Lead times respond to steel availability rather than labour.
assumption: Core steel is the binding transformer input.
kill: Lead times shorten while steel stays tight.

channel: Transfer capacity moves power between regions and flattens price spreads.
condition: The link is built and operated.
assumption: Regional price differences exceed transfer cost.
kill: Spreads persist after the link operates.

channel: A permitted site still needs a substation to be usable.
condition: Substations are on the critical path to occupancy.
assumption: Switchgear cannot be stockpiled far ahead of the design.
kill: Sites occupy while substations lag.

channel: A long lag to recovery makes utilities sequence spend carefully.
condition: Cash flow, not desire, governs the plan.
assumption: Utilities cannot fund indefinite working capital gaps.
kill: Plans accelerate while recovery lags.

channel: A higher allowed return makes more projects worth building.
condition: The project earns the allowed return on the spend.
assumption: Rate base growth is the utility objective function.
kill: Capex plans shrink when allowed returns rise.

channel: Hardening spend uses the same equipment and crews as growth.
condition: Both programmes draw on the same supply chain.
assumption: Hardening is mandatory and cannot be deferred.
kill: Growth capex accelerates while hardening spend rises.

channel: A visible backlog is the political trigger for reform.
condition: Backlog is measured and published.
assumption: Regulators respond to documented delay.
kill: Reform is passed while backlogs fall.

channel: Power delays keep the installed base scarce and spreads wide.
condition: Providers must energise to earn.
assumption: Rental prices clear on availability.
kill: Spreads narrow while transformer delays run long.

channel: Core steel is the long pole in transformer output.
condition: Mills run near capacity and new lines take years.
assumption: Core steel cannot be imported at scale under current duties.
kill: Lead times fall while steel capacity is flat.

channel: Conductor designs trade copper for aluminium as prices diverge.
condition: Design codes permit aluminium in the relevant applications.
assumption: Substitution is technically acceptable and persistent.
kill: Substitution reverses when the price gap narrows.

channel: Cable is a copper intensive, long lead item.
condition: Cable demand is incremental rather than reshuffled.
assumption: Mine supply cannot respond inside the project window.
kill: Cable lead times fall while copper tightens.

channel: Generators and turbines need magnets and castings together.
condition: Both inputs are needed for the same unit.
assumption: Neither input has a fast substitute.
kill: Units ship with one input missing.

channel: SiC devices change converter and breaker designs.
condition: Qualification cycles complete and designs adopt the parts.
assumption: Reliability in the field matches incumbent technology.
kill: Adoption stalls on qualification failures.

channel: Batteries smooth on site generation and shift load.
condition: Storage is part of the on site design.
assumption: Anode supply is the battery constraint.
kill: On site projects proceed without storage.

channel: Closed loops need chemistries that survive high heat flux.
condition: Retrofit specifications depend on the coolant.
assumption: The chemistry is available at industrial scale.
kill: Retrofits stall on fluid supply or rules.

channel: Firm nuclear power needs fuel contracts that reach years ahead.
condition: Enrichment capacity is contracted before restart.
assumption: Fuel supply is not substitutable inside the restart window.
kill: Restarts proceed while fuel coverage is short.

channel: Electrical steel and castings compete for the same industrial capacity and power.
condition: Both are made in heavy industrial clusters.
assumption: Clusters cannot expand power and labour quickly.
kill: Both lines expand together without constraint.

channel: Plans are only as fast as the crews that build them.
condition: Crews are the binding constraint rather than equipment.
assumption: Crews cannot be imported or trained inside the plan window.
kill: Plans execute faster than crew availability allows.

channel: Energization work needs licensed electricians in a narrow window.
condition: Fitout labour is the last gate before energization.
assumption: The trade cannot be substituted by equipment.
kill: Sites energize faster than electrician availability allows.

channel: Casting capacity decides how many turbine slots become machines.
condition: Specialist castings are on the critical path.
assumption: Casting capacity cannot be expanded quickly.
kill: Turbines ship at booked rates despite casting constraints.

channel: Higher wages attract crews but raise the cost of every project.
condition: Wage increases do attract labour into the trade.
assumption: The labour supply responds to wages within the cycle.
kill: Wages rise and crew availability does not improve.

channel: A growing backlog pulls crews to the biggest projects.
condition: Backlog is real work rather than options.
assumption: Crews move toward the highest bidder.
kill: Backlogs grow while crew supply comes free.

channel: Contractor backlogs are the earliest public read on provider spend.
condition: Contractors book before providers report capex.
assumption: Backlog converts to revenue rather than being cancelled.
kill: Backlogs build while provider capex falls.

channel: A queue position without land is not a project.
condition: Sites must be entitled before they can be studied.
assumption: Entitlement is on the critical path rather than parallel.
kill: Projects proceed to construction before entitlement.

channel: Organised opposition converts permits into litigation.
condition: Opposition has standing in the process.
assumption: Local politics can delay but not permanently block.
kill: Projects with active opposition proceed on schedule.

channel: The permit is what makes the water usable.
condition: Water law binds before physics does.
assumption: Rights are not transferable at the needed scale.
kill: Sites with water constraints run evaporative cooling anyway.

channel: Fibre routes define which places can be close enough.
condition: Latency depends on path, not straight line distance.
assumption: New routes are not built inside the site window.
kill: Sites are chosen without regard to route availability.

channel: Latency critical tenants sign long contracts near users.
condition: Tenants pay a premium for proximity.
assumption: Proximity cannot be replicated elsewhere.
kill: Tenants accept remote sites for latency critical work.

channel: Water stress triggers consumption rules.
condition: Local supply is the political trigger.
assumption: Rules bind the site rather than being waived.
kill: Rules tighten while supply recovers.

channel: Limits force the retrofit decision.
condition: Retrofit is permitted and supply constrained only by capital.
assumption: Closed loop designs meet the limit at acceptable cost.
kill: Limits are imposed and no retrofit activity follows.

channel: Retrofits add capex per megawatt on top of the base build.
condition: Retrofit spend is provider funded.
assumption: The retrofit cannot be passed to the tenant in full.
kill: Retrofits are tenant funded and leave provider capex flat.

channel: Visible community benefit softens local resistance.
condition: The benefit is legible to the community.
assumption: Opposition responds to material benefits rather than identity.
kill: Reuse projects do not change local approval.

channel: On site plants need cooling too, and change the water balance.
condition: The generation design includes cooling.
assumption: On site plants are not air cooled where water is scarce.
kill: On site plants add water stress without any constraint.

channel: Opposition to grid build makes self generation attractive.
condition: Grid capacity is contested locally.
assumption: Self generation avoids the contested permitting path.
kill: Opposition subsides and on site building continues.

channel: Higher rates compress the multiple on the same cash flow.
condition: Duration of the cash flows exceeds the rate move horizon.
assumption: The multiple is primarily a discount rate story rather than a growth story.
kill: Multiples expand while rates rise.

channel: Wider spreads shut the securitisation window and slow the build.
condition: Deals clear on spread rather than on structure.
assumption: Securitisation is a marginal funding source rather than the core one.
kill: Issuance continues at the same pace through a spread shock.

channel: Securitisation lets lessors fund fleets against contracted cash flows.
condition: Contracts are assignable and rated.
assumption: Investors accept equipment and contract risk at the offered spread.
kill: Lessors fund only with equity and their growth stalls.

channel: Vendor credit terms are a read on end demand strength.
condition: Vendors use credit to clear inventory.
assumption: Vendor financing expands when demand softens, not when it surges.
kill: Terms tighten while lead times lengthen.

channel: Cheap capital lets landlords buy sites ahead of demand and entitle them.
condition: Development is funded on the balance sheet.
assumption: Landlords can carry entitled land through the permitting period.
kill: Site acquisition stops when cost of capital rises.

channel: The schedule decides reported earnings for the same cash flow.
condition: The market prices reported earnings rather than cash flow at the margin.
assumption: Depreciation policy is not fully transparent to the market.
kill: Multiples are unchanged by depreciation policy changes.

channel: Accounting decides what counts as contracted revenue and committed cost.
condition: Leases are material enough to change the reported picture.
assumption: Disclosure is comparable across issuers.
kill: Reported contracted share moves with accounting rather than contracts.

channel: Cheap money feeds the cycle; expensive money cuts the flow.
condition: Credit conditions bind on marginal projects.
assumption: The cycle is funding driven rather than demand driven at the margin.
kill: Capital inflow accelerates while rates rise.

channel: Spread widening forces the marginal owner to sell into weakness.
condition: Leverage is high enough that refinancing matters.
assumption: Lenders mark and manage exposure actively.
kill: Spread widening has no effect on asset sales.

channel: Credits pull spending forward into the qualifying window.
condition: Projects qualify and can be placed in service in time.
assumption: The credit is a marginal subsidy rather than the only reason.
kill: Credits are enacted and no acceleration follows.

channel: Tariffs on transformers and steel raise cost and stretch delivery.
condition: Tariffs bind on the imported alternative.
assumption: Domestic supply cannot replace imports inside the window.
kill: Lead times fall while tariffs rise.

channel: Reform can compress the study and approval clock.
condition: Reform binds on the binding step.
assumption: Agency capacity exists to implement the change.
kill: Clocks are unchanged after reform takes effect.

channel: Caps remove the scarcity signal that would attract generation.
condition: Caps bind in scarcity hours.
assumption: Merchant revenue is the entry signal.
kill: Entry continues while caps are binding.

channel: Localisation mandates create long sovereign contracts.
condition: Compliance requires in country capacity.
assumption: Providers can serve the mandate at a return.
kill: Sovereign contracts are announced and not signed.

channel: Scrutiny slows consolidation exactly when it is cheapest.
condition: Deals need clearance in the relevant jurisdictions.
assumption: Distressed assets cannot be carved out without review.
kill: Consolidation proceeds unimpeded during scrutiny.

channel: Subsidies raise the return that attracts capital.
condition: The credit flows to the marginal project.
assumption: Capital is responsive to after tax returns.
kill: Capital flows in without credits.

channel: Wide spreads justify more spend on capacity.
condition: The spread is expected to persist past the payback.
assumption: Providers reinvest retained spread rather than returning it.
kill: Spreads widen and spending falls.

channel: Spending ahead of revenue compresses near term earnings and multiples.
condition: Depreciation and interest land inside the measurement window.
assumption: The market charges near term earnings rather than rewarding capacity.
kill: Multiples rise with intensity, as the asset growth literature once implied.

channel: A few large tenants set price and terms.
condition: Tenants can threaten to self build.
assumption: Concentration is durable rather than temporary.
kill: Spreads widen while concentration rises.

channel: Contracted cash flows are what makes a deal financeable.
condition: Contracts are long enough to cover the debt tenor.
assumption: Investors price contract quality rather than counterparty identity.
kill: Deals fund fully on merchant exposure.

channel: The market prices the cash flow per unit of capacity.
condition: Capacity data is disclosed consistently.
assumption: Revenue per megawatt is the cleanest read of pricing power.
kill: Multiples track total revenue while revenue per megawatt falls.

channel: Discipline shows up as slower intensity growth.
condition: Buyers have genuine alternatives to deploying capital.
assumption: Discipline survives competitive pressure.
kill: Intensity keeps rising through a stated discipline phase.

channel: New independent capacity competes the spread down.
condition: Capacity arrives in the same demand window.
assumption: Neocloud capacity is price competitive for the same workloads.
kill: Spreads stay wide while independent capacity scales.

channel: A higher multiple is cheaper equity and easier funding.
condition: Equity issuance is a live funding channel.
assumption: Management issues into strength.
kill: Raises stop while multiples rise.

channel: Intensity funded on balance sheet pushes providers toward fewer, larger tenants.
condition: Balance sheet funding requires anchor contracts.
assumption: Anchor contracts are compatible with the tenant base.
kill: Intensity rises while the tenant base diversifies.

channel: A visible shock pulls capital into the theme.
condition: The shock is legible to capital markets.
assumption: Capital chases the theme rather than the asset.
kill: Capital stays out while the shock is obvious.

channel: Funded capacity gets built, and it arrives in herds.
condition: Capital converts to physical capacity within the cycle.
assumption: Builders cannot coordinate to stop at demand.
kill: Capacity additions track demand without overshoot.

channel: Excess capacity clears at prices below full cost.
condition: Demand does not grow into the new capacity in time.
assumption: Supply is price inelastic downward.
kill: Prices hold while utilisation falls.

channel: Distress transfers assets to the strongest balance sheets.
condition: Leverage exists to force sales.
assumption: Buyers have capital and conviction at the bottom.
kill: Distress appears with no consolidation.

channel: The leaner cost base makes new demand profitable.
condition: Demand persists across the cycle.
assumption: The surviving cost structure is genuinely lower.
kill: Second wave demand arrives at the old cost base.

channel: The second wave tightens the market again from a lower base.
condition: Capacity was retired or absorbed during the shakeout.
assumption: Demand growth outpaces the remaining capacity.
kill: Spreads stay depressed into the second wave.

channel: The crowded short side exists precisely in the overbuild fear.
condition: Positioning data shows crowding.
assumption: Fundamentals and positioning diverge enough to squeeze.
kill: No squeeze occurs despite crowding.

channel: Forced selling consumes resting depth and widens spreads.
condition: The forced account is large relative to the book.
assumption: Depth does not replenish inside the window.
kill: Spreads tighten during forced selling.

channel: Depth is the capacity limit that turns a shock into a dislocation.
condition: Depth is measured at the moment it matters.
assumption: Displayed depth is a usable estimate of executable size.
kill: Deep markets dislocate as much as thin ones.

channel: Dealer hedging adds or removes depth depending on the strike structure.
condition: Dealer gamma has the same sign as price moves.
assumption: Hedging flows are visible in depth rather than hidden in dark venues.
kill: Depth is unchanged by option positioning.

channel: Passive flows are mechanical and price insensitive.
condition: Inclusion dates are known and flows are predictable.
assumption: Index funds trade the close regardless of price.
kill: Inclusion has no volume or price effect.

channel: Squeezes move the multiple without changing the cash flow.
condition: Short interest is high enough to move price.
assumption: Fundamentals do not resolve inside the squeeze window.
kill: Multiples move with cash flow only.

channel: Dislocations created by forced flow can revert once the flow ends.
condition: The forced seller is finite and identifiable after the fact.
assumption: The dislocation is larger than the cost of taking the other side.
kill: Dislocations continue without reversal.

channel: Firm nuclear contracts displace new gas for the same capacity need.
condition: Nuclear restarts or new builds clear their own permits.
assumption: The nuclear tranche is additive supply rather than a reshuffle of existing output.
kill: Gas slots keep booking at the same rate while nuclear contracts grow.

channel: Behind the meter supply removes load from the scarcity calculation.
condition: The load is genuinely islanded or contractually curtailable.
assumption: On site capacity is not double counted as system capacity.
kill: Scarcity prices rise while self generation scales.

channel: Conductor substitution changes the copper intensity per kilometre.
condition: Codes and designs accept aluminium for the application.
assumption: Substitution is persistent rather than a temporary squeeze response.
kill: Copper intensity per kilometre is unchanged by the price gap.

channel: Efficient conversion and storage arrive together in the same site designs.
condition: Designs include both conversion and storage.
assumption: Neither component substitutes for the other.
kill: Sites add one without the other at scale.

channel: In house silicon consumes the same limited memory bits.
condition: ASICs use comparable memory content per unit of compute.
assumption: Substitution shifts vendors rather than relieving the memory constraint.
kill: HBM tightness eases while ASIC volume grows.

channel: Vendor credit and securitisation are alternative ways to carry the receivable.
condition: Both channels are open to the same buyer.
assumption: Buyers use the cheaper channel rather than both.
kill: Both channels deepen at the same time for the same buyer.

channel: Latency requires a path, and paths follow fibre.
condition: Latency critical workloads dominate the site decision.
assumption: Fibre routes cannot be built inside the decision window.
kill: Sites are placed for latency without regard to fibre availability.

channel: Volume growth fills rented capacity before it fills new capacity.
condition: Installed capacity has spare utilisation.
assumption: Providers can raise price on the installed base.
kill: Spreads fall while token volume grows.

channel: Consumer bursts hit the same pools as enterprise workloads and price clears the peak.
condition: Consumer demand is bursty and shares capacity with paid workloads.
assumption: Providers do not reserve capacity for one segment only.
kill: Consumer spikes leave rental prices unchanged.

channel: Enterprise workloads want fixed prices and long terms.
condition: Enterprises are willing to sign multi year commitments.
assumption: Providers prefer contracts to spot exposure.
kill: Contracted share stays flat while enterprise adoption grows.

channel: Training contracts are large but finite and renegotiated each generation.
condition: Training buyers keep optionality rather than locking capacity.
assumption: Frontier scale changes fast enough that long contracts are unattractive.
kill: Training contracts lengthen while scale keeps changing.

channel: Sovereign buyers build rather than rent at scale.
condition: Programmes fund their own capacity.
assumption: Sovereign demand is additive rather than rented.
kill: Sovereign programmes rent at scale from listed providers.

channel: Cheaper tokens per watt reduce capacity per unit of output.
condition: Efficiency converts into lower capacity needs rather than more usage.
assumption: Elasticity does not absorb the efficiency gain inside the window.
kill: Spreads hold while efficiency improves sharply.

channel: Long lead times force prepayment and inventory, both of which hit the capex line.
condition: Vendors require commitments and deposits.
assumption: Prepayment is treated as capex rather than working capital.
kill: Capex intensity falls while lead times lengthen.

channel: Lenders underwrite the fleet against residual value.
condition: Residual value is the collateral in the structure.
assumption: Residuals are observable and enforceable.
kill: Funding terms are unchanged by residual values.

channel: Restricted markets buy through cloud region workarounds, tightening available supply elsewhere.
condition: Workarounds exist and are used.
assumption: The workaround demand is served from the same pools.
kill: Restricted demand drains without affecting rental prices.

channel: Wafers gate finished parts when packaging is available.
condition: Wafer capacity is the tighter of the two constraints in the window.
assumption: Node capacity cannot be reallocated quickly from other products.
kill: Lead times fall while node utilisation is full.

channel: Cluster networking is a rising share of the bill of materials.
condition: Clusters scale in port count faster than in compute per node.
assumption: Optics are provider funded rather than tenant funded.
kill: Networking cost per unit of compute falls.

channel: Power cost is a direct deduction from the revenue a megawatt can earn.
condition: Provider power contracts are floating rather than fixed.
assumption: Providers cannot pass the full move to tenants in the short run.
kill: Revenue per megawatt is unchanged by power prices.

channel: Capacity revenue is a contracted stream that can be sold forward.
condition: Provider generation is capacity accredited.
assumption: The stream is financeable.
kill: Capacity revenue is excluded from contracted share by the market.

channel: Faster connections add capacity and narrow spreads.
condition: Reform delivers megawatts inside the cycle.
assumption: Added capacity is not offset by new queue entries in the same window.
kill: Spreads stay wide while connections accelerate.

channel: Cancellations free turbine slots for the next buyer.
condition: Slots are cancellable with penalty.
assumption: Cancelled slots are re-marketable.
kill: Slot queues lengthen through an overbuild.

channel: Excess capacity defers the next wave of grid spend.
condition: Utilities respond to load forecasts that fall with cancellations.
assumption: Load forecasts are revised rather than sticky.
kill: Capex plans accelerate through an overbuild.

channel: Funding closes when the price signal breaks.
condition: Lenders and equity are return sensitive.
assumption: Distressed terms do not attract new capacity in the same window.
kill: Funding opens wider during a price collapse.

channel: Consolidation shrinks the order book that kept crews busy.
condition: Cancellations exceed new awards.
assumption: Contractors release crews rather than hoard them.
kill: Backlogs grow through the shakeout.

channel: The second wave competes for the same crews at a lower price point.
condition: The cost base is lower but the labour pool did not grow.
assumption: Crews return from other sectors.
kill: Crew scarcity is absent in the second wave.

channel: Demand converts into site acquisition and entitlements.
condition: Capital exists to buy land ahead of demand.
assumption: Entitlement queues are the binding step.
kill: Site acquisition is flat while demand shocks upward.

channel: Higher rates raise the revenue requirement and the political resistance to it.
condition: Rate cases pass the cost of capital through to consumers.
assumption: Political tolerance for bill increases is finite.
kill: Capex plans grow as rates rise.

channel: Expensive credit kills the marginal self generation project first.
condition: On site projects are project financed.
assumption: Balance sheet funding is not available instead.
kill: Self generation accelerates through a credit shock.

channel: Cheap REIT capital is deployed against long leases, so the mix shifts with funding.
condition: REITs compete for the same tenants as providers.
assumption: Funding cost decides who wins the tenant.
kill: The funding mix is unrelated to the contract mix.

channel: Securitisation lets the marginal builder keep building past the point of sense.
condition: Deals clear on contracted cash flows regardless of market-wide capacity.
assumption: Rating agencies do not aggregate sector exposure fast enough.
kill: Issuance closes before the overbuild arrives.

channel: Tariffs on conductor and rod redirect sourcing and cost.
condition: Tariffs bind on the imported alternative.
assumption: Domestic supply is not instantly substitutable.
kill: Sourcing and cost are unchanged by the tariff.

channel: Localisation forces capacity into jurisdictions with weaker grids.
condition: The jurisdiction lacks grid headroom.
assumption: On site generation is permitted locally.
kill: Localised capacity waits for the grid without building.

channel: Scrutiny makes the largest contracts and their terms public.
condition: Inquiries produce disclosures.
assumption: The market reads the contracts through the inquiry.
kill: Contract terms are unaffected by scrutiny.

channel: Caps push large loads to build rather than buy.
condition: Caps are binding and durable.
assumption: Self generation is permitted.
kill: Loads keep buying capped power without building.

channel: If permits shorten and lead times do not, the bottleneck was never permits.
condition: Both clocks are measured.
assumption: Equipment lead times are independent of permitting.
kill: Lead times shorten when permits shorten.

channel: Forced selling in related equities and private marks moves the reference prices for residuals.
condition: Residual values are marked against market references.
assumption: Marks adjust faster than disposal prices.
kill: Residual marks are unchanged by forced selling.

channel: Dealer hedging absorbs buying pressure and flattens multiple expansion.
condition: Positioning is concentrated at strikes near spot.
assumption: Dealers hedge rather than warehouse.
kill: Multiple expansion is unaffected by option positioning.

channel: Index inclusion lowers the cost of equity for the included name.
condition: The name is included in a major index.
assumption: Passive demand is price insensitive at the margin.
kill: Funding access is unchanged by index events.

channel: Thin books make the same fundamental news produce larger multiple moves.
condition: Depth is thin relative to the news flow.
assumption: The marginal price setter is small relative to the float.
kill: Multiple moves are independent of depth.

channel: When power is gated, the spend is only in the money if the delay is shorter than the demand curve.
condition: Delays are long relative to the demand cycle.
assumption: Demand persists past the delay window rather than moving to another site.
kill: Providers keep spending into delays that outlast the demand.

channel: Elasticity is the moderator that decides whether rental prices fall on new supply.
condition: Elasticity is above one and new supply arrives.
assumption: New supply serves elastic demand rather than displacing the installed base.
kill: Prices collapse on new supply even with elastic demand.

channel: Rate direction decides whether intensity is punished or ignored.
condition: The measurement window spans a rate move.
assumption: Multiple compression dominates the capacity reward in the window.
kill: Intensity is rewarded in every rate regime.

channel: Thin public markets cannot fund the cycle at the needed scale, so private capital decides.
condition: Equity issuance exceeds what the book absorbs.
assumption: Private and public capital are substitutes.
kill: The cycle funds itself entirely in public markets regardless of depth.

channel: Wage pressure only changes behaviour when the allowed return does not cover it.
condition: Rate cases lag wage settlements.
assumption: Regulators do not pre-emptively raise allowed returns.
kill: Utilities absorb wage increases without re-filing.

channel: Steel scarcity matters more where tariffs close the import valve.
condition: Tariffs bind on core steel imports.
assumption: Domestic mill capacity cannot respond inside the window.
kill: Lead times fall after tariffs despite tight steel.
